sentence: The invoices table on the billing page is hard to scan once there are more than twenty rows.

reviewer_notes.codebase_facts: Next.js 15.3 app router, React 19, Tailwind v4 CSS-first @theme inline, shadcn new-york/zinc primitives (Table/Badge/Button/Card/Dialog), Geist Sans + Geist Mono via next/font, light-first :root with .dark opt-in, left rail (hidden <md) + top header, settings sub-nav tabs, radius 0.5rem, table rows h-10 header / py-2 cells, Lucide icons.
reviewer_notes.existing_invoice_table: components/billing/invoice-history.tsx: 6 fixture rows, columns Invoice (mono id) / Issued / Period / Amount / Status / Download; responsive column hiding sm/md; status badge with icon + label; no sticky header, no grouping, no pagination, no sort, no exception-first ordering, no zebra/row banding.
reviewer_notes.what_a_good_answer_does: Keep the same Table primitive and column set; make 20+ rows scannable: sticky/pinned header, exceptions (open / past due) surfaced first or grouped, tighter fixed row height, tabular numerals already present, year grouping or a paginate/show-more with a row count, optional status filter chips, mono id kept; no virtualization (20-100 rows), no inline edit, no bulk selection, do not change navigation/theme/typography.
reviewer_notes.fixture_note: Fixture has only 6 invoices; to reproduce the task the fixture will be extended to ~30 rows (data change, recorded under before/).
